why_ai: Unlicensed rights trading protected by filmmaker and buyer relationships and hard acquisition bets, while streamers and aggregators bypass the middle and rights admin automates.
why_clarity: Box office is measured, but whether a bid was good is a taste call graded years later across scattered statements.
why_digital: Films, contracts and statements are digital and licences are delivered remotely, but acquisitions happen in festival rooms and markets.

why_ai: Each festival bid is a novel, high-stakes call on one viewing, sold to filmmakers on the buyer's taste and reputation.
why_clarity: Opening weekends arrive fast but ultimates take years, and buyers price by feel on 10-30 bids a year.
why_digital: Models and campaigns run on screen, but films are judged in festival theatres and won through face-to-face bidding.

why_ai: Territory sales run on long relationships with buyers met at markets, though estimates and avails work is automatable.
why_clarity: Closed deals give a checkable price per territory, but estimates are set by feel and graded a season later.
why_digital: Rights and materials move digitally worldwide, but selling still happens in market meetings.

why_ai: Settlement calculation and reconciliation automate readily, leaving only the negotiation with circuit buyers.
why_clarity: Terms and grosses define an exact amount owed per engagement, repeated hundreds of times a release.
why_digital: Grosses and statements are data and invoices are digital, with terms agreed by phone with known buyers.

why_ai: Clause extraction and avails logic are exactly what language models and rules engines now do, with legal exposure keeping a reviewer.
why_clarity: An avails answer is checkable against the contracts, and the same questions recur constantly.
why_digital: Contracts in, structured grants and answers out, all on screen.

why_ai: Statement checking against contract terms automates, while claims and negotiation keep accountants and lawyers involved.
why_clarity: Fee bases, caps and receipts give a recomputable answer, though expense allocation is often opaque.
why_digital: Agreements and statements are documents reviewed remotely.

why_ai: Licensing transactions automate, but catalogue coverage rests on studio relationships and venues' trust in a known agency.
why_clarity: Each licence is a defined product per title, venue and date, sold in large volume.
why_digital: Catalogues and licences are online, but the screenings happen in physical venues bought through local institutions.

why_ai: Servicing, delivery and scheduling of library titles are mechanical, and only licence pricing keeps judgement in play.
why_clarity: Revenue per title is measurable and recurs monthly, though licence pricing is negotiated.
why_digital: Titles, metadata and reports move digitally between holders and platforms.

why_ai: Delivery, ad-break marking and channel scheduling at thousands of titles are directly automatable.
why_clarity: Viewing minutes and ad revenue per title arrive weekly as objective feedback.
why_digital: Files, metadata and schedules delivered to platforms entirely online.

why_ai: Senior sellers' knowledge of each buyer's ceiling is relational, though comparables and ranges can be modelled.
why_clarity: Final prices are exact, but pricing is by feel and deals are confidential and infrequent per buyer.
why_digital: Deals done remotely with platforms, with relationships built at markets.

why_ai: Shot search and quoting automate, but authentic historical footage is the one thing generative video can't supply.
why_clarity: A request is satisfied by a specific clearable clip, and licences recur daily.
why_digital: Footage, search and licences delivered online to producers anywhere.

why_ai: Fingerprinting and takedown are machine-scale work, with adversarial pirates and legal enforcement keeping analysts.
why_clarity: A match is infringing or not and takedowns succeed or fail quickly, at enormous volume.
why_digital: Content monitored and enforced entirely online.

why_ai: Accountants sign audit claims and testify, and statement disputes persist whatever tools distributors adopt.
why_clarity: Contract terms make most findings checkable, though settlements are negotiated and slow.
why_digital: Statements and records reviewed on screen, with clients found through entertainment relationships.

why_ai: Recruited screenings need people in theatres and studios trust established norms, though survey analysis automates.
why_clarity: Scores are standard and repeated per film, and the opening weekend grades the forecast within weeks.
why_digital: Live audiences and surveys feed reports delivered digitally to studio research teams.

why_ai: Signal collection and demand modelling are exactly what AI analytics produces, so the vendor's edge is its history.
why_clarity: Demand indices are repeatable, but whether a valuation was right is rarely observed.
why_digital: Online signals in, dashboards and valuations out.

why_ai: Exhibitor-reported grosses form an institutional currency that AI cannot recreate, though collection is automated.
why_clarity: Grosses are exact counts reported daily for every theatre.
why_digital: POS data in, reports out, sold to a concentrated industry.

why_ai: The board's authority, not the viewing labour, is what distributors pay for, though classification models now assist.
why_clarity: Guidelines codify most decisions over ~700 films a year, with appeals as the check.
why_digital: Films submitted and rated digitally, by a single authority per territory.

why_ai: Forecasting from box office history is model work AI does directly, leaving the analyst's industry read.
why_clarity: Every forecast is graded by actual grosses within days.
why_digital: Licensed data in, forecasts and briefings out online.

why_ai: Internal forecasting and pricing support automate, while dating and window strategy stay with executives.
why_clarity: Window revenue is measurable and recurs, but release strategy questions vary film to film.
why_digital: Revenue and rights data analysed on screen inside firms.

why_ai: Configurable software whose own functions are being rebuilt around language-model extraction.
why_clarity: Grants, windows and royalties follow defined rules that the software checks.
why_digital: Software sold and implemented remotely to rights holders.

why_ai: Neutral fiduciary administration is a trusted role, but statement processing automates.
why_clarity: The waterfall defines exact payouts, repeated every distribution period.
why_digital: Receipts, statements and payments handled electronically across territories.

why_ai: Credit decisions on films are relationship-driven and carry institutional accountability.
why_clarity: Loans are repaid or not, but outcomes take years and each film differs.
why_digital: Collateral and documents are digital, deals sourced through industry relationships.

why_ai: Running a physical market and an arbitration tribunal depends on member trust and in-person convening.
why_clarity: Model contracts are codified, but market and policy outcomes are hard to measure.
why_digital: Member data and contracts are digital, but the market itself is in person.

why_ai: Directory maintenance and deal scraping are directly automatable.
why_clarity: Listings are complete and current or not, maintained continuously.
why_digital: Listings in, searchable database out by subscription.
